articles.title: Maresca eyes rest for busy dad Haaland as Manchester City prepare for Porto
articles.summary: Norwegian forward has played every minute of season. Parenting duties have changed player’s ‘priorities’ Enzo Maresca believes Erling Haaland has become “complete” as his priorities have changed after the birth of the Manchester City No 9’s son two years ago.
body: Haaland has again started the campaign in prolific form, scoring three goals in City’s opening three Premier League victories. In three of the 26‑year‑old’s four previous seasons at City he has won the Premier League golden boot. Maresca pointed to how the birth of his son in 2024 changed the Norwegian’s motivation.

The manager said: “He’s a man now. He’s a dad. When he arrived here [in summer 2022] he was not a dad and now he’s a dad and life completely changes because the priority becomes his son. I’m happy for him because he was already top as a player and as a boy but now you can see that he is complete. He is a family man, he is still scoring goals so I’m very happy for him.”

City are at Porto in the opening league‑phase game of the Champions League on Tuesday. Haaland has played every competitive minute of the campaign so far, and Maresca said he will be rested at some point, particularly as as the striker was part of the Norway team that reached the World Cup quarter-finals.

articles.title: Belichick denies he has lost control of UNC football program amid off-field turmoil
articles.summary: Former general manager has resigned post. Belichick’s son Steve is on medical leave. School has launched investigation into program. North Carolina football coach Bill Belichick said on Monday he believes his program “totally” has an atmosphere of following rules amid an investigation into its…
body: “Obviously everybody’s responsible, including me, for doing things properly,” Belichick said. “And we intend to do that.”

The Tar Heels were off following their season-opening win against TCU in Ireland on 29 August. But during that open week, general manager Michael Lombardi resigned after being put on paid administrative leave in late July amid the university’s investigation into his conduct.

The same day, Raleigh TV station WRAL cited anonymous sources in reporting the type of questions asked of some interviewees. Some focused on Belichick’s son Steve, the Tar Heels’ defensive coordinator, who is currently on medical leave. There have also been allegations that Steve Belichick has been questioned by lawyers over issues related to drug use.

Additionally, Lombardi attorney Tom Mars told The Athletic that the school’s investigation now included questions into potential “inappropriate” relationships that didn’t involve his client. Two people with knowledge of the situation had previously told the AP that a human resources complaint from a former employee was tied to Lombardi originally being placed on leave as the investigation launched.

articles.title: Emery ready to ignite Aston Villa’s season at Club Brugge after familiar slow start
articles.summary: Manager remains calm despite his side taking one point and scoring no goals in opening three Premier League games. Unai Emery is not panicking. He may kick every ball on the touchline but, behind closed doors, Aston Villa’s players are used to him being the calmest person in the room, routinely…
body: Emery, McGinn and Villa have been here before. Just last season, in fact; at this point, they were pointless in the Premier Leagueand still another 157 minutes from registering their first goal. So in one sense Villa, who shook off a slow start to qualify for the Champions League for the second time in three seasons, are ahead of schedule. Villa’s goalless draw at Hull on Saturday was not the most absorbing display but there were enough green shoots to trust Emery when he says he is confident they can again exceed expectations.

It is hard to disbelieve a man with Emery’s record, having overseen the most successful era in the club’s recent history. “When we started the project here, the ambition we had, it was [not even] in our highest expectations to be in Europe four years in a row,” the Villa manager says. “It was very difficult when we started working together but it was the ambition of the owner. We set our standards high with the players to be there and we are. Now is the moment to remember how we got here and the way we did. Now it is a different moment and chapter.”

articles.title: Zheng Qinwen erases another 5-0 deficit to stun Swiatek and reach US Open quarter-finals
articles.summary: Zheng makes astonishing recovery to win 7-5, 6-3. Rybakina sweeps aside Osaka 6-1, 6-4 to set up clash. The most important takeaway from 12 days at the US Open is simple: do not, by any means, lead 5-0 against Zheng Qinwen. No scoreline is as hazardous.
body: Somehow, two days later, Zheng repeated the trick in her very next set against a greater opponent. Down 5-0 in the opening set of her fourth‑round match against the six-time grand slam title winner Iga Swiatek, Zheng again locked down her game and reeled off seven games in a row to take the set. Zheng refused to let it go as she pulled off one of the best wins of her career, reaching the US Open quarter‑finals with a 7-5, 6-3 victory.

This was a remarkable turn of events for a variety of reasons. A player winning seven games in a row from 0-5 down in consecutive sets against two different opponents is almost unheard of at the highest level; doing so against two grand slam title winners has never happened before.
“In one moment, I even forgot the score in the first set at 4-5,” Zheng said. “That shows how I am focused. I guess, to come back 0-5 [again] is not lucky, that’s [what] I can say.”

articles.title: Rich Paul Explains Why Stephen Curry Should Get A Profit Share And Stock Options With Warriors
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors superstar Stephen Curry is among the most popular figures in the sporting world today. While he is primarily known for his exploits on the basketball court, there is no denying the impact he has had on the Warriors behind the scenes.
body: Stephen Curry’s gradual rise to superstar status has been vital to the Warriors’ growth as a franchise. With Curry’s “brand” drawing in more fan support and driving more revenue, Golden State has benefited greatly from him donning the jersey. But should he be rewarded for this?

“You know, in Fortune 500 or Fortune 100 companies, and you are an executive at a specific level, you get stock and things like that, and that’s able to grow and compound over time… You [players] cannot invest in a team, but they do have a direct correlation to a team’s compounding in terms of value… All players aren’t created equal in this situation. But in someone like Steph’s case, he definitely moves the needle when it pertains to the value of an organization.”

“From his pre-game warm-up routine, which has value, all the way to his production, to his play on the floor night in and night out. And then, when you add on factors like his showmanship, his professionalism, and things of that nature, absolutely.”

articles.title: Waterdogs’ rookies help send Philadelphia back to PLL Championship
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Waterdogs defeated the Boston Cannons 13-10 on Monday at Zions Bank Stadium, earning a trip to the PLL U.S. Bank Championship on Sept. 20 against the Denver Outlaws. The story wasn’t a perfect performance.
body: The story wasn’t a perfect performance. It was Philadelphia’s ability to absorb Boston’s best punches without losing its identity.

“We found so many different ways to win games,” CJ Kirst said. “We faced adversity today. There were so many highs, so many lows. But yet again, we had the confidence to go out there and play our game.”

Despite a rocky start, Philly’s defense settled in behind rookie goalkeeper Sean Byrne. After the Cannons’ first two goals, Boston missed 18 of its final 19 shots of the first half, going 19 minutes without scoring.
Byrne finished the game with 14 saves and 10 scores allowed in his first PLL playoff appearance.

But England's Lines, 31, compiled breaks of 77 and 84 to win the next two frames and set up a last-32 meeting with Yuan Sijun in Brentwood.
"You try not to think about it, but you know if you don't play somewhere near your best then you are going home."

articles.title: Dan Campbell Reveals Lions’ Plan Behind Jahmyr Gibbs
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions lost their intended No. 2 running back before the season even started. Dan Campbell’s answer is not to find another one. With Isiah Pacheco on injured reserve, Detroit will open the season with Jahmyr Gibbs at the center of the backfield and Sione Vaki and Jacob Saylors sharing…
body: “It’s by committee,” Campbell said. “I see Vaki getting some reps too. I don’t see it like Saylors is running back 2.”
That distinction matters because it tells us something about Detroit’s plan for Gibbs, too.

Pacheco was supposed to provide veteran support behind Gibbs after Detroit reshaped its backfield during the offseason. Instead, a back injury landed him on injured reserve, meaning he will miss at least the first four games.

The easy conclusion would be that Saylors simply slides into Pacheco’s spot. His preseason made a pretty convincing argument. Saylors consistently produced when given opportunities and had already taken control of Detroit’s final running back competition before eventually earning a place on the roster.

articles.title: Rybakina too strong for Osaka as Zheng stuns Swiatek at US Open
articles.summary: Elena Rybakina cruised into the US Open quarter-finals with a straight-sets victory over Naomi Osaka to keep her push for the world No 1 ranking on track.
body: Rybakina will reclaim the top spot if she reaches the semi-finals, and after dismantling two-time champion Osaka on Louis Armstrong, she has every reason to believe she can go all the way and lift the US Open trophy.
It took the second seed just over 20 minutes to wrap up the first set 6-1 before securing a decisive break midway through the second to quell a resurgent Osaka and seal an emphatic 6-1 6-4 victory.

"I played really well today. I was feeling the ball was really good from my side," the former Wimbledon champion said. "I was a bit lucky in some moments, found some lines, but super happy with the performance.
"Naomi is a tough opponent. I knew no matter the score I needed to focus on each ball as everything can change quickly. She is also a great player. I am glad how I played today.

articles.title: Usyk's camp dismiss Fury's offer to be 'backup plan' for Joshua fight
articles.summary: Oleksandr Usyk's manager has dismissed Tyson Fury's call for a third fight with the Ukrainian amid continued doubt over an all-British heavyweight showdown with Anthony Joshua.
body: With protracted negotiations over a long-awaited Fury-Joshua bout being held up by a dispute over where the fight would take place, Fury took to social media on Monday to say he was looking for a new opponent.
Fury said he wants a third fight with Usyk, who became undisputed heavyweight champion as he beat Fury twice on points in 2024.
Responding to Fury's comments in a statement given to Sky Sports News on Monday evening, Usyk's manager Sergey Lapin said: "Usyk is not Tyson's backup plan.
"If Fury needs an opponent, he should visit the Ready to Fight platform. They can help him find a worthy opponent there.

articles.title: SMU-Florida State Kicked Off With Only Some Lights, No Replay After Power Outage
articles.summary: Florida State and No. 19 SMU kicked off at 9:15 p.m. ET at Doak Campbell Stadium following a nearly two-hour power outage that forced both programs to play under severely restricted conditions.
body: As teams prepared to take the field, ESPN reported that the game would proceed despite significant operational limitations. According to Yahoo Sports, the two programs kicked off without full stadium lights, working public address speakers, referee microphones, sideline iPads, coach-to-player helmet communications, or functioning scoreboards.
Officials said that the Seminoles (1-0) and Mustangs (0-0) were to take the field at 9 p.m. for warmups with a 9:15 p.m. ET kickoff, almost two hours after the scheduled 7:30 p.m. ET kickoff.

A statement on the Jumbotron inside Doak Campbell Stadium at 8:30 p.m. read: "Technical staff are addressing a power disruption to the west side tower due to an electrical short in the main transformer. Electricians are working to restore the power service. The game remains suspended. Update to follow."

ACC commissioner Jim Phillips chatted with athletic directors from both schools, SMU’s Damon Evans and Florida State’s Michael Alford, for a few minutes on the field before administrators moved inside to further discuss options.
